plugin.name: Jujutsu VCS Integration
plugin.description:
Native IntelliJ integration for Jujutsu (jj), a Git-compatible version control system with a fundamentally different approach to working with code.

Why Jujutsu?

Jujutsu treats your working copy as a commit—always. No staging area, no "dirty" state. Just describe what you're working on and keep coding.

Key Features

  • Describe-First Workflow — Working Copy tool window for describing current work and creating new changes.
  • Custom Log View — Visual commit graph with inline change IDs, descriptions, and bookmarks.
  • Change Operations — Edit, abandon, and describe changes directly from the log.
  • File History & Annotations — Full file history with diff viewer and line-by-line blame.
  • Multi-Repository Support — Work with multiple JJ repositories in a single project.
  • Real-Time Status — Auto-refresh keeps the UI in sync as you edit files.

GitHub · Issues
plugin.change-notes:
0.8.19

Added

  • **Push Tag** is now in the right-click menu of a tag chip in the log and of a tag in the Bookmarks panel (a submenu when there are several remotes). It runs `jj git push --tag` after a confirmation prompt, and needs jj 0.44 or later — on older versions the item stays visible but disabled, and Settings lists it under Feature Availability. ([#124](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/124))
  • The Working Copy panel's changes toolbar gained a **Restore** button, next to Resolve all conflicts, pre-checking whatever's selected in the tree (or opening empty for the current repo when nothing's selected). "Restore" and "Restore to This" now read "Restore…"/"Restore to This…", since both open a dialog rather than acting immediately. ([#84](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/84))
  • The log toolbar gained a **Revset** filter chip alongside Reference/Author/Date/Root: type any jj revset (click the chip, Enter to apply) to narrow the graph to it, combined (AND) with every other active filter. Resolved client-side against the loaded entries, so it never changes what's fetched from jj for this or any other open tab. An invalid revset shows jj's own error inline without losing the chip's last-good filter; a filter that matches commits outside the currently loaded window says so in the status bar instead of just looking short. Persisted per log tab. ([#116](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/116))
  • **Split into New Parent…** is now in the log's right-click menu, right below **Split into New Child…**, instead of only being reachable from the file-tree menu. It opens the same dialog: ticked files move to a new commit inserted before the selected one, which keeps its own change ID. ([#132](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/132))
  • Accepting a side for several conflicted files at once is now a single jj operation with an **Undo** link in the confirmation balloon, so one click reverts the whole selection instead of only the last file.
  • **Bookmark Ahead/Behind Counts** in the log's View Options menu hides the ↑n↓m numbers on bookmark chips in the log and the Bookmarks panel (a collapsed folder with unsynced bookmarks keeps a plain `•` marker, and hover tooltips still show the counts). On by default; applies to every project. ([#128](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/128))

    • Fixed

  • Splitting with **Pick Hunks…** no longer turns a file deletion you left unticked into an empty file: the deletion now lands in the first commit as a real deletion, and a ticked deletion still moves to the new commit.
  • Multi-selecting conflicted files that name the same two commits in opposite order now shows a coherent pair of accept labels (e.g. "Accept change B" / "Accept change A") instead of the generic "Side #1"/"Side #2", and accepting one resolves every file to that same commit.
  • Developers with the DevKit plugin no longer hit an `IllegalArgumentException` (`TextRange.allOf`) while the IDE indexes the plugin's `JujutsuBundle.properties`: the unused `plugin.description` key had a shape DevKit parses as a plugin-id reference with no id. ([#100](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/100))
  • Pushing a bookmark backwards or sideways (a force push) or pushing a bookmark deletion no longer skips its confirmation prompt with recent jj releases (0.44 and later). jj changed the wording of its push preview (`bookmark: main [move sideways from … to …]`), which the plugin no longer recognised; both the old and new wording are now understood, and a push preview the plugin can't read is logged.
  • A bookmark's ↑n/↓m ahead/behind arrows on the log table's chips could keep showing the previous numbers after a Refresh, only catching up on a second Refresh: the log rows and the bookmark data reload in parallel, and the rows could finish first and pick up the old counts. The chips now update as soon as the fresh bookmark data arrives. ([#128](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/128))
  • With a Diff Base other than "Working copy parent", editor gutter change markers disappeared entirely for a file added after the base (e.g. added in an ancestor change, with the base set to the latest immutable ancestor). Such files now diff against an empty base, so every line shows as added. ([#133](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/133))
  • When jj is merely slow to answer (a busy system makes the 30-second working-copy read time out), the plugin no longer says the repository "could not be read… may be broken, moved, or created by an incompatible version of jj", turns the VCS mapping red, or blanks the Working Copy panel. It now shows a "Jujutsu Is Not Responding" notification with a Retry action and keeps the last-known working copy; the Working Copy panel says "Loading Jujutsu repositories, please wait..." during the first load (instead of "No Jujutsu repositories configured") and explains a timeout, and its messages now wrap instead of being cut off. ([#123](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/123))
  • Auto-refresh now works in secondary jj workspaces (`jj workspace add`). Previously the plugin watched a `.jj/repo/op_heads` folder that only exists in the primary workspace, so jj commands run in a terminal never refreshed the log, bookmarks or working copy there. ([#115](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/115))
  • Squashing, rebasing or duplicating many changes at once no longer pushes the destination picker off the bottom of the dialog: the source list at the top now scrolls within about five rows, and shorter lists look exactly as before. ([#125](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/125))
  • A per-repo override of Log Revset or Log Limit in Settings didn't update any open log window until the toolbar Refresh button was clicked — the setting change wasn't reaching the log panel at all in the common case, and, separately, once paged log loading was enabled its lightweight per-write refresh path kept reusing the previous revset/limit until an explicit Refresh rebuilt it from scratch. Both now take effect as soon as you click OK/Apply.
  • Abandoning a non-empty change or one with a description already asked for confirmation, but abandoning an *empty*, undescribed change that carried a bookmark silently deleted the bookmark along with it, since `jj abandon` removes local bookmarks pointing at the abandoned revision. The confirmation dialog now also fires in that case and names the bookmark(s) that would be deleted. ([#129](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/129))
  • At any IDE zoom other than 100%, icons in the commit details panel, row tooltips and bookmarks panel sat too high or too low and overlapped (or left a gap before) the text after them, and bookmark/tag chip names didn't scale with the zoom at all. Icons and chips now size and line up the same way as in the log table.
  • Selecting and copying text in the commit details panel or a tooltip now includes bookmark/tag names, the author's `Name ` and dates — previously each of these copied as a blank space.

    • See full release notes for details.
